title: Graded fallthrough and on-call guidance for load prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We've seen periodic surge events where noisy downstreams and regional capacity pressure cause a flood of alerts and noisy on-call activity. Existing hard circuit breakers cause abrupt failovers that spike latency for critical customers and create a deluge of pages. Goal: introduce a graded fallthrough mechanism plus on-call guidance to prioritize load during contention so we reduce page noise while preserving critical request progressions to SLA-bound customers.

Scope: design and implement a 2-stage circuit gating policy (soft gate -> hard gate) with load-priority buckets, update SLO burn analysis and alert thresholds to be context-aware, and author a concise on-call playbook with automated remediation primitives. This ticket covers policy design, console routing knobs, runbook text, and one automation play (auto-degrade non-critical routes on sustained soft-gate conditions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Circuit gating policy documented and code prototype merged behind feature flag.
- Alert rules tuned so we drop non-actionable pages by >=60% in the Canary cluster during simulated surges.
- On-call playbook published in Confluence and linked from the alert.
- One automated remediation (non-critical route degrade) implemented and tested in staging with rollback path.
- Dashboard showing per-route SLO burn, gating state transitions, and pages_by_route per hour.

Design summary:
- SLO model: use 3-window burn (1m, 5m, 1h) weighted scoring to estimate immediate and sustained stress.
- Load prioritization: routes annotated with priority labels (critical, standard, best-effort). Requests from best-effort routes will be targeted for early shedding.
- Graded gating:
  - Soft gate: when 1m burn > threshold AND 5m burn trending up -> switch to soft gate. Soft gate triggers internal response headers and increments a 'shed_score' for best-effort routes; also reduces sampling of verbose traces and suppresses low-signal alerts (400/429 surge alerts) from paging.
  - Hard gate: triggered when 5m burn and 1h burn exceed stricter thresholds or when internal circuit error rate exceeds X%. Hard gate starts active failover to alternate region or cheaper model variant and opens a P0 path for critical routes only.
- Alerting logic: move from static thresholds to composite alert rules that require gating state AND owner-impacting metrics. Lower-priority alerts become informational or routed to a 'Recovery' Slack channel instead of on-call.
- Runbook: step-by-step for soft->hard transition, how to triage false positives, and manual overrides. Automations include an idempotent 'degrade-route' job and a reversible capacity-shed toggle.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive shedding reduces pages but can impact throughput for paying customers; mitigated by strict prioritization and explicit opt-out per route.
- Complexity of multi-window burn increases alerting fidelity but adds computational cost to the routing layer; we will pilot with sampling and lightweight counters before full rollout.
- Automations risk flapping; we include hysteresis windows and cooldown timers to prevent oscillation.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged prototype in staging (this sprint).
2) Canary in us-west-2 with low-traffic tenants and dashboarding for 72h.
3) Evaluate metric targets and adjust thresholds.
4) Gradual enablement for more tenants and final toggle for automation.

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic surge tests using chaos-runner to verify >=60% reduction in noisy pages while keeping critical p99 latency within SLO envelope.
- Backfill-run on historical incidents to estimate false positive/negative behavior.
- BL-compare of unit economics: measure tokens/second cost delta during shed events.

Open questions / next steps:
- Exact numeric thresholds for soft vs hard gates (proposal in design doc; needs SRE sign-off).
- Whether to expose route opt-out to customers via Console (work for later cycle).
- Integrate with Dedicated capacity routing policies for customers with reserved capacity.
